news.title: Markets Brace for August Tariff Deadline
news.text: Global equities began July with restrained trading on July 1-2 as investors assessed the outlook for trade negotiations ahead of the August 1 tariff deadline.

news.title: U.S.-Vietnam Trade Deal Lifts Wall Street
news.text: The United States and Vietnam reached a trade agreement on July 3, propelling the Dow Jones up 0.77%, the S&P 500 up 0.83%, and the Nasdaq up 1.02% to new record closes.

news.title: Independence Day Market Closure
news.text: U.S. markets were closed from July 4-6 for the Independence Day holiday weekend, providing a quiet stretch for global trading.

news.title: Solid Jobs Data Meets Trade Jitters
news.text: Positive U.S. payroll data showing 147,000 new jobs and a 4.1% unemployment rate on July 7 was offset by tariff concerns, leaving the Dow Jones down 0.16% and the S&P 500 down 0.3%.

news.title: Tariff Pause Sparks Global Rally
news.text: The U.S. President temporarily paused tariffs for 14 trading partners on July 8, igniting rallies across Asian and UK markets.

news.title: Momentum Builds After Tariff Reprieve
news.text: Markets extended gains on July 9 as investors continued to welcome the temporary suspension of new tariffs.

news.title: FTSE 100 Climbs to 9,000
news.text: Energy and mining stocks helped the FTSE 100 reach a record 9,000 points on July 10 amid renewed optimism about global trade.

news.title: Late-Week Trade Focus
news.text: From July 11-13, markets stayed fixated on the trajectory of U.S. trade negotiations heading into mid-July.

news.title: Tariff Threat Pressures Europe
news.text: European equities slipped on July 14 after the U.S. President warned that 30% tariffs could be imposed on EU imports if an agreement was not secured by August, sending the Stoxx 600 down 0.6%.

news.title: FTSE 100 Finds Support
news.text: On July 15, the FTSE 100 inched up 0.2%, aided by the UK's existing trade deal with the United States even as tariff risks lingered elsewhere.

news.title: Markets Consolidate Mid-July
news.text: Markets experienced limited catalysts between July 16-22, consolidating while digesting sector developments and a 3% estimate for U.S. Q2 GDP growth.

news.title: U.S.-Japan Deal Boosts Nikkei
news.text: A breakthrough trade agreement between the United States and Japan on July 23 sent the Nikkei surging 3.75%, highlighted by strong gains in automakers.

news.title: Optimism Builds After Japan Pact
news.text: July 24-27 trading reflected improved sentiment as investors anticipated additional trade progress following the U.S.-Japan agreement.

news.title: U.S.-EU Deal Avoids Major Tariffs
news.text: On July 28, the United States and European Union struck a trade deal that prevented the looming 30% tariff and set a 15% baseline, lifting EU indices roughly 0.8%-1%.

news.title: Markets Build on Trade Clarity
news.text: European and U.S. markets continued to enjoy momentum on July 29 as investors digested clearer trade rules.

news.title: Tariffs Announced on Indian Goods
news.text: Fresh 25% tariffs on all goods from India were announced on July 30, weighing on Indian equities as investors assessed supply chain implications.

news.title: Strong Close to July on AI Strength
news.text: Stocks ended July higher on July 31 supported by AI leaders, while the Federal Reserve maintained interest rates at 4.25%-4.50%.

news.title: Executive Order Triggers Tariff Shock
news.text: At the start of August, a U.S. executive order allowing reciprocal tariffs up to 41% rattled Asian markets, pushing South Korea's KOSPI down 3% and Japan's Nikkei down 0.4%.

news.title: Soft Jobs Data Pulls Yields Lower
news.text: U.S. Treasury yields slid on August 4 after a weak July payrolls report and downward revisions increased expectations for a September Federal Reserve rate cut, helping the S&P 500 advance.

news.title: FTSE 100 Notches Fresh Highs
news.text: Between August 5-6 the FTSE 100 added 0.24% to new highs while U.S. tech outperformed on news of a major Apple domestic investment that sent its shares up 5.1%.

news.title: Earnings Strength Lifts Wall Street
news.text: U.S. stocks climbed on August 7 as Apple's momentum and upbeat corporate reports from names such as McDonald's pushed the Nasdaq up 1.2% and the S&P 500 up 0.7%.

news.title: Tariff Legal Battle Adds Volatility
news.text: Markets swung on August 8 amid tariff debates and mixed earnings after a U.S. appeals court ruled sweeping reciprocal tariffs illegal but delayed enforcement, contributing to U.S. equity declines and choppy gold prices.

news.title: Europe Eyes U.S.-Russia Talks
news.text: European stocks edged up 0.3% on August 11 as investors awaited U.S.-Russia talks that spurred tentative hopes for progress in Ukraine.

news.title: Nasdaq Sets New High on Tech Surge
news.text: Technology and growth names powered the Nasdaq Composite to 21,681 points on August 12, underscoring investor confidence in AI-driven earnings.

news.title: Global Index Hits Record High
news.text: On August 13 the MSCI All Country World Index reached a new peak as traders priced in a higher probability of U.S. rate cuts.

news.title: Peace Hopes Cool Defence Stocks
news.text: Speculation about a Russia-Ukraine peace breakthrough on August 19 drove the Stoxx 600 up 0.6% while defence shares lagged on de-escalation expectations.

news.title: UK Inflation Surprise Fails to Stall Rally
news.text: Despite July inflation running at 3.8%, the FTSE 100 advanced 0.67% on August 20, marking yet another record high.

news.title: Dow Jones Hits Record Close
news.text: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at a record on August 22 before moderating later in the month as investors rotated across sectors.

news.title: Oil Rallies on Russia Supply Fears
news.text: Concerns about Russian exports drove Brent crude to $68.80 per barrel on August 25, supporting energy shares.

news.title: Dow Extends Records, Europe Wobbles
news.text: The Dow secured another record close on August 28, while French equities weakened on worries about potential government instability.

news.title: Tariff Scope Widens for U.S. Imports
news.text: Markets finished the week cautiously on August 29 after the United States ended the de minimis tariff exemption, broadening levies on consumer goods ahead of the Fed's September meeting.

news.title: Labor Day Market Closure
news.text: U.S. exchanges were closed on September 1 in observance of Labor Day, resulting in muted global volumes.

news.title: Record Gold Signals Investor Nerves
news.text: Gold prices touched a record $3,508.50 per ounce on September 2 as UK, European, and U.S. indices slipped, with the FTSE 100 down 0.43% and the S&P 500 off 1.2%.

news.title: Markets Await U.S. Data
news.text: Caution prevailed on September 3 ahead of key U.S. releases while energy traders focused on upcoming oil inventory data.

news.title: Airlines Slide on Jet2 Warning
news.text: Airline shares dropped on September 4 after Jet2 cut its profit outlook, dragging peers such as easyJet and IAG lower and wiping 14% from Jet2 stock.

news.title: Markets Poised for Payrolls
news.text: Equities treaded water on September 5 as investors awaited a rebound in U.S. non-farm payrolls following July's softness.

news.title: Trade Sensitivity Persists
news.text: On September 8 markets stayed sensitive to trade developments as Chinese export growth to the U.S. slowed.

news.title: AI Optimism Supports Tech
news.text: Tech stocks remained resilient on September 9 with U.S. investors upbeat about continued AI investment.

news.title: S&P 500 and Nasdaq Break Records
news.text: Major U.S. benchmarks hit new closing highs on September 10, underscoring broad strength ahead of the Federal Reserve meeting.

news.title: Rate-Cut Hopes Lift Wall Street
news.text: Expectations for a Federal Reserve rate cut on September 11 lifted the Dow Jones by 0.5% and pushed defence names like BAE Systems up 2.9% amid geopolitical tensions.

news.title: ECB Holds Rates Steady
news.text: The European Central Bank kept its policy rate at 2% on September 12, prompting a muted response from regional equity markets.

news.title: Alphabet Joins $3 Trillion Club
news.text: Alphabet shares surged nearly 4% on September 15, briefly valuing the company at $3 trillion for the first time.

news.title: Fed Cut Expectations Build
news.text: Markets on September 16 priced in a high likelihood of a Federal Reserve rate cut at the upcoming meeting.

news.title: Fed Delivers First 2025 Rate Cut
news.text: The Federal Reserve trimmed rates by 25 basis points to a 4.00%-4.25% target on September 17, with gold rallying toward $3,700 per ounce.

news.title: Post-Fed Consolidation
news.text: From September 18-23 markets consolidated gains, monitoring political developments such as instability in the French government.

news.title: Defence Stocks Jump on NATO Remarks
news.text: European defence names rallied on September 24 after the U.S. President suggested NATO aircraft should intercept Russian planes violating its airspace.

news.title: U.S. Equities Extend Pullback
news.text: Major U.S. indices posted a third straight decline on September 25 as investors reassessed valuations.

news.title: Pharma Shares Hit by Tariff Threat
news.text: Markets digested a September 26 plan for 100% tariffs on medicines and 25%-50% duties on other goods effective October 1, knocking AstraZeneca shares down 1.4%.

news.title: Robinhood Surges on Guidance
news.text: Robinhood shares jumped over 12% on September 29 after the CEO highlighted strong prediction-market performance, while President Trump met lawmakers to avert a shutdown.

news.title: Markets Look Past Funding Deadline
news.text: On September 30 investors stayed focused on the interest-rate path despite the looming U.S. funding deadline, as manufacturing PMI printed at 52.

news.title: FTSE 100 Opens October at Record
news.text: The FTSE 100 set a fresh record on October 1, making AstraZeneca the most valuable UK-listed company.

news.title: Global Equities Extend Highs
news.text: European and U.S. benchmarks added to gains on October 2, with the Stoxx 600 up 0.7% and the S&P 500 opening 0.3% higher.

news.title: Pre-Data Caution Settles In
news.text: From October 3-5 markets turned mixed as traders awaited key U.S. macro releases heading into the weekend.

news.title: France Political Shake-Up Hits CAC 40
news.text: The CAC 40 fell 1.8% on October 6 after the resignation of French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu, who lasted less than a month.

news.title: U.S. Equities Rebound After Volatility
news.text: Momentum-driven buying on October 7 helped U.S. stocks recover from earlier swings.

news.title: Gold Surpasses $4,000
news.text: Gold broke above $4,000 per ounce on October 8 as investors sought safe havens amid elevated geopolitical risk.

news.title: AI Enthusiasm Keeps Tech Rallying
news.text: Technology shares continued to gain on October 9 as enthusiasm for artificial intelligence remained robust.

news.title: Markets Mixed Amid Political Uncertainty
news.text: Between October 10-12 equities were mixed as investors weighed France's political turmoil and the risk of a U.S. government shutdown.

news.title: U.S.-China Tensions Pressure Asia
news.text: Asian stocks dipped on October 13 after Washington and Beijing exchanged fresh tariff threats.

news.title: Earnings Season and Lower Yields Support Markets
news.text: Markets consolidated between October 14-16 as corporate earnings season began and U.S. Treasury yields declined on rising rate-cut expectations.

news.title: Banking Sell-Off Hits U.S. and Europe
news.text: Credit concerns on October 17 sparked a sell-off in regional banks, pulling the S&P 500 down 1.2% and erasing nearly £11 billion from UK bank valuations.

news.title: Markets Await Japanese Political Outcomes
news.text: Caution set in on October 20 as investors watched Japanese political developments for potential policy changes.

news.title: Japan Elects First Female Prime Minister
news.text: Japanese equities rebounded on October 21 after Sanae Takaichi won the premiership on promises of looser fiscal policy.

news.title: Quiet Session for Major Markets
news.text: October 22 saw limited market-moving news, with traders awaiting the next catalysts.

news.title: Sanctions Lift Energy Shares
news.text: The United States announced fresh sanctions on Russia on October 23, boosting Brent crude and lifting UK energy majors BP and Shell by 3.5%.

news.title: Global Benchmarks Set New Records
news.text: Following a favorable inflation report on October 24, the FTSE 100 surpassed 9,600 for the first time while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq also posted new highs.

news.title: Markets Ease After Big Gains
news.text: Stocks pulled back modestly on October 27 as investors digested the prior week's rally.

news.title: U.S. Indices Renew Record Highs
news.text: U.S. benchmarks closed at fresh records on October 28 amid ongoing strength in technology and energy names.

news.title: Tariff Concerns Resurface Late October
news.text: Markets turned cautious on October 29-30 on news of new U.S. tariffs targeting India alongside the looming government funding deadline.

news.title: October Ends with Strong Earnings and Fed Cut
news.text: Equities finished October on a firm footing on October 31 thanks to robust Q3 earnings and a Federal Reserve rate cut to 3.75%-4.00%.
